text:
Harper G: quick UX thread  chart axes + legend density + outlier handling. We get complaints that dashboards with p95 overlays and 10 series look cramped. Options?
Nico L: couple ideas: 1) compress axis unit to `/s` or `k/s` when values are large; 2) let users pin a verbose label. Prefer auto-si + tooltip expansion.
Ava D: auto-SI is neat but can confuse product folks who read 'k/s'. Suggest we show `/s` on-axis, and use an adaptive suffix in the legend like `req/s` or `req (k)/s` for very large numbers. Tooltip always: "Requests per second (req/s)".
Markus F: note: some customers run per-minute dashboards. Could we make the axis unit toggle prominent in the small panel header (per sec / per min / absolute)? Quick switch might reduce support noise.
Harper G: good call. We'll add a tiny control in the legend header: "Units: /s ▾". Default `/s`, but remembers per-user preference.
Nico L: about legend density: when smoothing is active we currently render both raw and smoothed with equal weight. Proposal: smoothed primary, raw collapsed as a smaller row with inline "Show raw" control. That keeps the chart compact.
Ava D: agree. Also make the collapsed raw visually subdued but still focusable. Add a tiny keyboard affordance: Tab to legend, Enter to expand raw.
Markus F: outlier handling question: product requested a "clean view" mode. Two implementations discussed: hard clip at percentile (affects y-scale) vs. visual sentinel + fade of isolated samples. I'm leaning sentinel+fade: add a faint marker for spiky points and visually fade them; keep raw values intact for hover and export.
Harper G: sentinel approach preserves facts while giving a visual cue. Microcopy for the toggle? Suggestions: "Fade isolated spikes" vs "Suppress spikes" vs "Outlier sentinel".
Nico L: prefer "De-emphasize outliers" with helper text: "Fade isolated spikes visually; values unchanged." Short and clear.
Ava D: accessibility: fading must not remove keyboard focus. Add aria-live messages: when toggled, announce "Outlier de-emphasis on". Also put a small textual caption above the chart when active: "Outlier de-emphasis enabled".
ScreenReaderBot: A11Y reminder: do not rely on opacity alone. Provide an offscreen description for each faded series point: e.g., "point at 2025-03-05 14:03 value 12 (de-emphasized)" when focused. Also ensure focus order doesn't skip faded points.
Markus F: implementation note: keep raw points in DOM, apply `.point--deemphasized { opacity: 0.25; stroke-width: 1px; }` and `pointer-events: auto` so hover works. For clipped mode (opt-in emergency), only alter scale when user explicitly enables "Clip outliers (affects scale)" with a clear warning.
Harper G: legend behavior: collapsed raw entry should show a chevron and readout like "Raw (hidden)". Use aria-expanded on the row. Keyboard shortcut idea: `L` to focus legend, arrow keys to move, Space to toggle collapsed state. Document in the shortcuts help.
Nico L: tooltip copy: sentence case please — "Requests per second (req/s)". Also include a small line when outlier de-emphasis is active: "Outlier de-emphasis: on" so screenshots are explicit.
Ava D: tiny UI copy nit: helper text must be <80 chars for small panels. Proposed helper: "Fade isolated spikes visually; values unchanged." (55 chars).
Markus F: QA/rollout: behind feature flag `console.featureFlags.outlierDeemphasis`. Start internal beta, watch for support tickets about missing spikes. Provide a toggle to switch to clipping if users prefer.
Harper G: action items: I'll update Figma with three variants (no de-emphasis, de-emphasis, clipped) and mock legend collapsed state. I'll open a PR with prop `deEmphasizeOutliers: boolean` and feature flag. Add aria strings and keyboard tests.
ScreenReaderBot: test checklist: 1) aria-live announcement on toggle, 2) offscreen point descriptions for faded points, 3) legend row aria-expanded toggles, 4) keyboard nav tests.
Harper G: thanks all — I'll post the figma link and PR once ready. :mag:
